title: Fractional units and repeat()
learningObjectives: Explain fractional units and repeat() and use CSS Grid to create responsive two-dimensional layouts.

understand.concept: Grid's fr unit distributes available space among flexible tracks. repeat() repeats a track list or pattern and can be combined with auto-fill and auto-fit. Fractional tracks still respect track sizing constraints and minimum contributions.
understand.whyItMatters: Using repeat() reduces duplicated track definitions. Combine it with minmax() when cards need a minimum usable width but should expand to share available space.
understand.analogy: repeat() is a compact way to describe repeated lanes; fr shares the space remaining after other sizing contributions.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS Grid follows formal track sizing, placement, and alignment algorithms.

explain.narrative: The grid repeats two equal flexible columns. Change repeat(2,1fr) to repeat(3,1fr).

examples.explanation: The grid repeats two equal flexible columns. Change repeat(2,1fr) to repeat(3,1fr).
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered CSS Grid example demonstrating the topic.

practise.guidedTask: Create a card grid with repeat() and fr. Compare equal tracks with 1fr 2fr 1fr.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive card or dashboard layout using this concept. Test long labels and narrow viewports.
hints: Inspect grid tracks with browser developer tools.
Check implicit tracks and minimum sizing.
Keep DOM and keyboard reading order logical.

questions.prompt: What should a responsive Grid layout preserve?
options: Readable content and logical DOM order
A fixed number of columns at every width
Visual placement regardless of keyboard order
questions.answer: Readable content and logical DOM order
questions.explanation: Responsive layout should adapt while preserving access and meaningful reading order.
